text:
ELOIRE 1,000-unit commercial answer — draft ready, 6 answers needed from you.

Correction first: "Elores" is ELOIRE — Diana Aviles Rodriguez's dry shampoo brand. Not an aerosol job. Nothing in the record mentions aerosol or propellant; she refers only to the same bottle design as run 1. I made no aerosol capability claim.

What she actually asked (Outlook thread "ELOIRE Reorder – lead time & details", opened 2026-06-18, last message 2026-08-02): reorder lead time, MOQ, per-unit pricing at volume tiers, formula/design retention, the fix for scratched and spotted bottles from run 1, plus QC inspection and a damage replacement policy.

Gap: written pricing was promised six times (6/29, 7/6, 7/9, 7/22, 7/29, 7/31). On 8/2 she got only "Got the numbers — 8.20 Per unit" — no breakdown, no lead time, no packaging or QC answer, no credit policy.

Draft reply saved for your review, not sent: /tasklet/agent/home/contracts/drafts/ELIOR-1000-UNIT-COMMERCIAL-ANSWER.md

Six questions — one sentence each:
1. Does the $8.20/unit you already sent include packaging, fill/labor, and overhead, or is it ingredient/BOM only?
2. Actual current lead time to produce and ship 1,000 units of this SKU?
3. What specifically changed (vendor, packing material, inspection step) to fix the run-1 scratching and spotting?
4. Will the run get a pre-shipment cosmetic QC inspection, and who signs off?
5. What is PLL's real replacement/credit policy for units arriving damaged?
6. Standard bottle/pump fill confirmed — any aerosol component at all?

Flag: $8.20 went out with no cost breakdown, which is outside PLL quoting policy. If it is BOM-only we are exposed on a live number.

Note: CRM could not be searched — the dedicated consultant account is still pending approval. Findings are email-verified only.

Sam, one correction before anything else. Elores is Eloire, Diana's dry shampoo brand, and it is not an aerosol job. Nothing in the record mentions aerosol, so I did not promise her anything we may not be able to do.

She asked for lead time, minimum order, tiered pricing, the fix for the scratched bottles from her first run, and a damage policy. Written pricing was promised six separate times since late June, and on Sunday she got a single number, eight dollars twenty a unit, with no breakdown behind it.

I have the full reply drafted and waiting for your review. It is not sent.

I need six short answers from you, and the first one matters most. Is that eight twenty a fully loaded price, or is it ingredient cost only? If it is ingredient only, we have a live number in front of a customer that does not cover packaging, labor, or overhead.

My recommendation is that you answer question one today, and I will finish and send the rest of the quote around it.
